meta.description: Unload of outstanding authorization data from the IMS database into sequential GSAM output files for archiving or further processing.
meta.process_description: The program fully reads all outstanding credit card authorization records from a hierarchical IMS database. It processes a two-level hierarchy: for each authorization summary record (summary/root segment, e.g., account information), all associated authorization detail records (child segments) are read. Both the summary records and the detail records are written to separate GSAM output files (Sequential Access Method for IMS), with the account key serving as the linking key. The program typically serves as the first step in a batch processing cycle to provide authorization data for downstream processes (e.g., cleanup, migration, reporting).

files.PAUTBPCB: IMS database access to the pending authorization database (source of authorization data)
files.PASFLPCB: GSAM output file for authorization summary records (summary/root segments)
files.PADFLPCB: GSAM output file for authorization detail records (child segments)
files.PAUTSUM0: IMS segment: summary of pending authorizations (root segment, per account)

business_rules: Only authorization summary records with a valid (numeric) account number (PA-ACCT-ID IS NUMERIC) are written to the output file and their detail records are processed.

The hierarchical relationship between account summary and authorization details is preserved: detail records are only read in the context of their parent summary record (GNP – Get Next within Parent).
In the event of a database error (status not equal to spaces or end-of-file), the program terminates with return code 16 (hard abend) to prevent data loss or inconsistent output.
The program processes all pending authorizations in full (Full Unload) without filtering by date or status – it is a complete data extract of the entire pending authorization database.
The checkpoint mechanism (RMAD prefix) is intended for batch restart capability, allowing the run to be resumed in the event of an abend.

Binds the GSAM output file for authorization detail records (child segments) into the IMS processing context.
Performs all preparatory steps for the batch run: initialization of counters, reading of control parameters (expiry period, checkpoint frequency), and positioning to the first database record.
Iteratively processes each pending authorization summary record (per account) from the IMS database and writes it together with its detail records to the output files.
Controls the processing loop: all accounts are processed until the entire pending authorization database has been completely unloaded.
After completion of the full data extract, properly closes the GSAM output files, thereby ensuring the integrity of the unloaded authorization data.
Terminates the batch run and returns control to the IMS batch controller after all authorization data has been completely unloaded.

variables.name: P-EXPIRY-DAYS
variables.description: Configuration parameter: Specifies the number of days after which a pending authorization is considered expired. Passed as a control value via the JCL-PARM, it determines the validity period of pending authorizations in the credit card system (e.g., 07 = 7 days). Authorizations older than this value can be identified for cleanup runs.

variables.name: FILLER
variables.description: Delimiter in the JCL-PARM string between P-EXPIRY-DAYS and P-CHKP-FREQ. A technically required filler byte (typically a comma or space) for correct positioning of the subsequent parameters in the input parameter buffer – has no independent business meaning.

variables.name: P-CHKP-FREQ
variables.description: Configuration parameter: Defines the checkpoint frequency of the batch run, i.e., after how many processed records an IMS checkpoint is set (e.g., '01000' = every 1,000 records). In the event of a program abend, this allows a restart from the last saved checkpoint so that already-processed authorization data does not need to be unloaded again.

variables.name: FILLER
variables.description: Delimiter in the JCL-PARM string between P-CHKP-FREQ and P-CHKP-DIS-FREQ. A technically required filler byte for correct positioning of the subsequent parameters – has no independent business meaning.

variables.name: P-CHKP-DIS-FREQ
variables.description: Configuration parameter: Controls the display frequency of checkpoint information in the batch log. Specifies after how many checkpoints a status message is written to the job log, making the progress of the unload run traceable for operators and administrators.

variables.name: FILLER
variables.description: Delimiter in the JCL-PARM string between P-CHKP-DIS-FREQ and P-DEBUG-FLAG. A technically required filler byte for correct positioning of the subsequent parameters – has no independent business meaning.

variables.name: P-DEBUG-FLAG
variables.description: Configuration parameter: Switch for activating debug mode for the batch unload run. Set via the JCL-PARM, it controls whether extended diagnostic and log output is generated during the processing of authorization data. Facilitates error analysis in test and production environments.

variables.name: DEBUG-ON
variables.description: Condition value: Signals that debug mode is active (P-DEBUG-FLAG = 'Y'). When this value is set, the program writes additional processing details – e.g., account numbers read, segment status codes, or counter values – to the job log to support traceability of the unload process.

variables.name: DEBUG-OFF
variables.description: Condition value: Signals that debug mode is inactive (P-DEBUG-FLAG = 'N'). In normal (production) operation, this value is set so that no additional diagnostic output is generated and the batch run executes efficiently without excessive log output.

variables.name: FILLER
variables.description: Trailing filler byte in the JCL-PARM input area after P-DEBUG-FLAG. Used to pad or delimit the parameter buffer to the expected total length – has no independent business meaning.

variables.name: PENDING-AUTH-SUMMARY
variables.description: Group field (record structure): Represents the working area for an authorization summary record (root segment PAUTSUM0) from the IMS pending authorization database. Contains account-level summary data such as account number (PA-ACCT-ID), credit limit, balance, and counters and amounts for approved and declined authorizations. Included via COPY CIPAUSMY and serves as the basis for each summary record written to the GSAM output file PASFLPCB.

variables.name: PENDING-AUTH-DETAILS
variables.description: Group field (record structure): Represents the working area for an individual authorization detail record (child segment PAUTDTL1) from the IMS pending authorization database. Contains transaction-level data such as the authorization key (date/time), card number, transaction amount, approval code, and merchant category. Included via COPY CIPAUDTY and serves as the basis for each detail record written to the GSAM output file PADFLPCB, always in the context of its parent summary record (GNP read strategy).

paragraphs.name: MAIN-PARA
paragraphs.description: MAIN-PARA is the central control framework of the batch run: it orchestrates the complete unload process of all pending credit card authorization data from the IMS database into the sequential output files.

paragraphs.name: 1000-INITIALIZE
paragraphs.description: Initializes the batch run for the authorization data unload process: the program captures the current processing date and logs the start event to the system log in order to document the beginning of the data extract in a traceable manner.

paragraphs.name: 1000-EXIT
paragraphs.description: Formal end point of the initialization section (1000-INIT). Serves as a structural terminator without its own business logic, enabling a controlled transition to the main processing loop of the authorization unload process.

paragraphs.name: 2000-FIND-NEXT-AUTH-SUMMARY
paragraphs.description: This paragraph retrieves the next pending authorization summary record (account root segment) from the IMS database and controls the complete processing of all associated authorization detail records for that account.

paragraphs.name: 2000-EXIT
paragraphs.description: Formal end point of processing block 2000, marking the return to the higher-level control logic of the unload process. This exit point terminates the read cycle of the pending authorization data in an orderly manner.

paragraphs.name: 3000-FIND-NEXT-AUTH-DTL
paragraphs.description: Retrieves the next authorization detail record (individual transaction) for the current account from the IMS database and writes it to the GSAM output file. Controls whether detail record loop processing continues or is terminated based on the result of the database access.

paragraphs.name: 3000-EXIT
paragraphs.description: Formal end point of processing block 3000, marking the end of the detail record read loop and returning control to the higher-level processing flow.

paragraphs.name: 3100-INSERT-PARENT-SEG-GSAM
paragraphs.description: Writes an authorization summary record (account root segment) to the GSAM output file for summary data. If a write error occurs, the batch run is immediately aborted to prevent inconsistent output data.

paragraphs.name: 3100-EXIT
paragraphs.description: Formal end point of the authorization detail record processing section (3100). Serves as a structural return point after all detail records for an account have been fully processed.

paragraphs.name: 3200-INSERT-CHILD-SEG-GSAM
paragraphs.description: Writes a single authorization detail record (e.g., a specific authorization transaction) to the GSAM output file for detail records. If a write error occurs, the batch run is immediately aborted to prevent inconsistent output data.

paragraphs.name: 3200-EXIT
paragraphs.description: Formal end point of processing section 3200, marking the end of the detail record processing loop and enabling the return to the higher-level account processing logic.

paragraphs.name: 4000-FILE-CLOSE
paragraphs.description: This paragraph closes the GSAM output files for summary and detail records after the complete data extract has finished. The actual close logic is currently disabled, as GSAM files in IMS are managed via the PCB mechanism and do not require an explicit CLOSE.

paragraphs.name: 4000-EXIT
paragraphs.description: Formal end point of the processing block for reading and unloading authorization detail records. Serves as a structural terminator without its own business logic.

paragraphs.name: 9999-ABEND
paragraphs.description: Emergency abort routine: in the event of a critical error (e.g., a database error), the batch run is terminated in a controlled manner to prevent data loss or inconsistent output in the authorization files.

paragraphs.name: 9999-EXIT
paragraphs.description: Formal end point of the program, signaling the orderly completion of the full pending authorization database extract and returning control to the calling batch process.
